data_migrations: Schema 41 → 42: the first time this version opens your library, it adds places for what this release can store, all empty to begin with: a program's start, end, lesson and arrival times, whether you archived it, which calendar event it was imported from and what the calendar import last saw of that event, the event rules it uses, a placeholder's saved search, and a dance's other titles, Barnes reference, meter, key, improper mark and interpreters, and what a square dance states about itself, such as its repeat order and whether it is a singing call. Event rules and interpreters get tables of their own. Nothing already in your library changes.

Taxonomy 39 → 40: contra gains the cast, hand cast and shift figures, the threes and fours as dancers, the previous and next neighbors' larks or robins as dancers, a second hand-hold for long waves and long waves that leave who faces in unstated, a Rory O'More in which one group slides two places, and pass by and pass through as one figure that can say who passes and where. No stored figure is changed, and the search index needs no rebuild of its own for it (it is rebuilt once for another reason, below).

On the first launch after updating, the app rebuilds its search index once, so that English figures and square calls your library may already hold (from a device on a newer version, a backup or a shared file) are found by their names. It also checks the text of your library once more, because this version keeps more kinds of text: as for everything you save, it removes invisible control characters and stores accented letters in one consistent form. Your dances are not otherwise changed.

Devices still on 0.10.x or older, and the dances you edit there: update every device before you convert or edit English or square dances. A device still on 0.10.x or older can't read a dance in one of the new English or square formations, or one whose phrases are named, so it keeps the copy it had before. If you edit that older copy there, even just a note or a rating, your edit replaces the newer version on all your devices, and its formation, named phrases, meter, key, other details and English or square figures are gone. Don't edit a program that names such a dance there either.

Devices still on 0.10.x or older show a contra figure whose dancers are the threes or fours, or the previous or next neighbors' larks or robins, with those dancers' internal names, such as "threes" or "next role1s". Opening that figure in the dance editor there and saving the dance replaces them with the default dancers, and that change syncs to all your devices, so update instead.

Devices still on 0.10.x or older show long waves that leave who faces in unstated as "unspecified facing in, others facing out", and opening that figure in the dance editor there and saving the dance fills in a facing the dance never stated, which syncs to all your devices. They show only the first hand-hold of long waves that state two.

Devices still on 0.10.x or older show a cast, hand cast or shift by its internal name, as an unknown move, and keep it as it is. They show English figures and square calls as unknown moves, and keep them as they are.

Devices still on 0.10.x or older show a Rory O'More without its "2 places", and a pass by or pass through that says who passes or where without it, or with the word "unspecified". A figure of your own that holds either is marked Needs repair there, and repairing it there can remove that detail from all your devices, so update instead.

English country dances stored before this version keep their contra moves and formation until you convert them: Settings ▸ General ▸ Import ▸ Convert English dances shows what would change in each dance and converts the ones you pick. Nothing converts them for you. Update every device first, because a converted dance gets an English formation.

A backup that holds an archived program or a program imported from your calendar is written as backup version 3, so versions 0.5.2 to 0.10.0 refuse to replace your library with it, instead of restoring your archived programs unarchived, or restoring imported programs without the calendar events they came from and offering those events again.

If you run your own sync server, update it before you update any device. This version sends things an older server refuses: new dance and program details, event rules, and new settings, such as the type of the last dance you added. Once the server refuses one, that device stops sending any of its changes, though it still receives the other devices' changes, and says "The sync server refused what this device sent." until the server is updated. Your changes stay safe on the device.
